description: We are an enthusiastic team passionate about space exploration, technology, science, and innovation. Our goal is to develop creative solutions using NASA’s open data to identify Earth locations similar to the Moon and Mars. We welcome motivated participants with skills in programming, AI, research, data analysis, and design. We believe teamwork, creativity, and collaboration can turn great ideas into meaningful solutions for the future of space exploration.
summary:
The Devon Project — Earth Analog Atlas
For 25 years, NASA has tested Mars missions on Devon Island — the most Mars-like place on Earth. But one island is not enough. Our project answers the question: where are the next hundred analog sites?
We developed the Earth Analog Atlas, an interactive web platform that identifies, scores, and compares terrestrial analog locations for permanent lunar bases and Mars missions. Built entirely on NASA open data — 30 years of NASA POWER climate records, ASTER GDEM elevation, and LRO/MRO mission archives — the atlas scores 12 sites across 8 dimensions of analogy (geology, terrain, temperature, water/ice, surface processes, biology, subsurface, and operations), separately for the Moon and Mars.
Because analogy is dimensional, not binary, our live weighting system lets users re-rank sites for their specific mission, and a Mission Planner recommends site portfolios with explicit "matches / does not match" reasoning. We also nominate 8 underexplored candidate regions — from an Indian basalt crater to unmapped Saudi lava tubes — flagged by NASA global datasets for scientific validation.
The atlas turns analog site selection from habit into evidence — openly, for everyone.
details:
Project Details

Our project aims to create new opportunities for students who are interested in space science and technology. It works by encouraging students to explore space-related topics, develop their knowledge, and take part in activities that support learning and innovation.

The project benefits students by helping them discover new interests, develop teamwork and problem-solving skills, and gain a better understanding of space science. Our intended impact is to build a strong and active student team that can inspire others and contribute to the future of Bahrain’s space sector.

To develop our project, we used digital tools, research, and technology to explore ideas and create our solution. Our team focused on creativity, teamwork, accessibility, and the needs of students interested in space.

What makes our project creative is its focus on giving students a chance to explore opportunities in space science and become part of a new generation of learners and future innovators. We hope our project will inspire more students to follow their passion and help support the growth of Bahrain’s space sector.
